x.tweet: Can you predict bit sequences better than a Bayesian that knows information theory? Three games. Real scores. Instant feedback.

vertical_caption: Can you outpredict a Bayesian on hidden bit patterns? Three games: guess the next bit, name the program, forecast probability. The Bayesian uses 2^(-L). You can swap in Thue-Morse or pi digits. Instant falsification 📊
shorts_description_lead: You versus a universal Bayesian predictor on bit streams. Guess the next bit, identify the hidden generator, or forecast probabilities. Real scoring, instant feedback.

video.title: Outsmart a Bayesian Predictor
video.script: Most of us think we're good at spotting patterns. But what happens when you're racing against a machine that literally knows information theory? Solomonoff Wordle puts you head-to-head with a universal Bayesian on bit sequences. Guess the next bit, identify the hidden program, or forecast the probability. The Bayesian uses 2^(-L) to weight hypotheses by their description length. Shorter programs, higher odds. Every bit you see, you both learn. Instant falsification. Play three modes, track your scores against the theory. Link in the description.
